pr_body:
Along the way, also trim `CoverageOptions` as part of the test trimming configuration, matching the logic in `TestConfiguration#SHOULD_INVALIDATE_FOR_OPTION_DIFF`. Also refactor `RunUnder` into a sealed interface implemented by two records.

Work towards #3325
Fixes #10782

RELNOTES: Changing any part of `--run_under` that isn't the label (such as the shell command) no longer invalidates the analysis cache.
pr_title: Preserve analysis cache through `--run_under` command changes
pr_comment:
@katre Assigning to you for review due to your work on Starlark option trimming, but feel free to delegate to someone else.

This PR consists of two commits, the first one of which is a pure refactoring. Let me know if you would prefer to review two separate PRs instead.
@katre Thanks, just keep in mind that I haven't rebased this onto #24318 after the latest changes.
@iancha1992 Could you mark this for cherry-picking into 8.1.0?

Unfortunately we are rolling this back: trimming CoverageOptions is problematic because it means that any attempt to transition coverage flags (such as `--coverage_output_generator` and `--coverage_report_generator`) will fail depending on whether or not the target is a test or not.

review_comment: Is it worth moving `--run_under` to a new `RunUnderOptions` class? Would that simplify things or make them more complicated?

I think that this doesn't simplify the situation as it would just introduce another one-of class that is involved in test trimming (`CoverageOptions` was already missed here). 

If we want to simplify this check, we could instead replace the `OptionDiffPredicate` concept with something less indirect. For example, we could just apply `TestTrimmingLogic.trim` to the old and new options and take the `OptionDiff` of that. That's almost straightforward except that we also need to take changes to `--experimental_retain_test_configuration_across_testonly` into account. I didn't want to do this in the current change.
Sounds reasonable, thanks for clarifying that.
